summary: Tested the family-pattern wife/husband split (structural only). Backend: I checked all 392 input combinations (3 wife lengths x 3 husband lengths x child 1/2) against the previous committed engine and table (git b559a27). There were 0 differences, and the baseline fixture also matches the old engine 392/392, so no prediction changed. All 61 master cases have the same wife/husband split and result as docs/source/pdf_transcription.json. Cases 30-40 are stored separately with origin old_app_only and do not appear in the PDF. A new live API test file passes 9/9: borrowed answers 75 and 72, not_in_table, exact 41 with duplicate_pattern, case 37 old_app_only with en/ar/de text (no raw keys), 15 random baseline pairs checked via the API, and History. The existing family-pattern unit and PDF tests pass 110/110 when REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is exported. Frontend (Clerk ticket session): wife Boy,Girl,Boy / husband Girl gives 'Table case #75', the 'Answer taken from table case #75 (Wife: Boy · Husband: Girl, Boy, Girl)' line and Boy. Wife Boy / husband Girl gives the 'Old App Only' badge next to Table case #37. The 3+3 Boy,Boy,Girl input gives Table case #1 with no source line and no badge. Arabic is RTL with all new labels translated and no horizontal overflow. German labels are translated. History lists family-pattern analyses with localized summaries. No page errors.

minor.issue: The test fails with MissingSchema (BASE_URL empty) unless REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is exported in the shell. Other live tests fall back to dotenv_values('/app/frontend/.env'); this one should do the same.

issues: The reference title ('Original family-pattern table (gender_prediction_logic.py, owner's legacy app)...') stays in English in AR and DE.
DE: the husband family label wraps to 2 lines, so the husband box sits slightly lower than the wife box (cosmetic).

action_items: Optional: make test_family_pattern_pdf_comparison.py read BASE_URL from /app/frontend/.env when the env var is missing
Optional: localize the family-pattern reference title for AR/DE
critical_code_review_comments: _pick logic is correct: it first looks for an exact wife/husband entry in legacy_order (source_line order), otherwise it uses the last joined-pattern match, which is the same later-wins behaviour as the old dict. Every duplicate pair (41/78, 42/75, 43/69, 44/72, 45/71, 46/76, 47/79, 48/70, 49/77, 52/73) has identical first and second answers, so the 'both entries give the same answer' text is accurate.

When the answer is borrowed, the header shows the case number twice ('Table case #75' and 'Answer taken from table case #75 ...'). This matches the spec but is redundant; consider showing only the source line.
Rate limiter is 30 analyses per minute per user, in memory and single worker (already documented).
seed_data_creation: None. Analyses created by tests were deleted by id (pytest fixture plus the 5 UI-created ids 6afb718d...646d to 6afb71e8...6471).

Run live pytest with -n 0 (pytest.ini adds xdist). The limit is 30 requests/min per user, so pace requests. /tmp/oldfp/compare.py shows how to compare against the old engine using git show b559a27.
